summary.headline: Molbio H1 FY27 revenue flat at INR667 crore (vs INR680 crore) as a one-month rate-contract delay shifts sales into H2; management reiterates 25% growth guidance.
summary.overview: H1 FY27 consolidated revenue from operations was INR667 crore versus INR680 crore in H1 FY26, with management attributing the softness to a roughly one-month delay in renewing the government rate contract. EBITDA was INR153 crore (23% of revenue), including a INR15 crore loss from OptraSCAN, and PAT was INR60 crore, lower on acquisition-related interest and intangible amortisation. The company moved to a net cash position by September 2026 from INR57 crore net debt in March 2026. Management said the lost month has been recovered in H2 and reiterated FY27 guidance of 25% top-line growth and a 24-25% EBITDA margin.

segments.name: Human molecular diagnostics (Truenat, TB and hepatitis)
segments.commentary: Revenue dip attributed to a one-month delay in government rate-contract renewal; management says orders are in hand and being shipped, and hepatitis B/C is in the national algorithm with a central procurement expected as a first-round order.

segments.name: OptraSCAN (US digital pathology, 60%-owned)
segments.commentary: Received US FDA approval about 2.5 months before the call; EBITDA loss of INR15 crore in H1 FY27. Management expects pickup in H2 but meaningful uptake from FY28.

segments.name: Radiology and veterinary
segments.commentary: Veterinary X-ray launched with early traction in regular and ultra-portable units; rabies Truenat test already in market; 6 further veterinary assays in development, targeted for FY28.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Export revenue about INR120 crore in H1 FY27; management expects more export activity in H2, including Global Fund-driven machine procurement.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance maintained: about 25% top-line growth and 24-25% EBITDA margin.
H1 typically 35-45% of full-year revenue; management cited a 40/60 H1/H2 split and expects the delayed month's revenue to land in H2.
OptraSCAN commercial contribution expected to pick up in H2 FY27, with real uptake from FY28.
Three new platforms (Truepoc, Trueamp, Truecyte) and veterinary Truenat assays expected in FY28; management said India CDSCO licence is about 4-5 months away and launches will be global.
capex_capacity: INR200 crore raised in the IPO, of which about INR72 crore is earmarked for automation; purchase orders already placed.
Management said automation can support about 3x the INR1,000 crore top-line level previously guided, so no further capex is needed for current growth.
Dhanraj Tolani cited about 58% kit and 42% device capacity utilisation; management did not directly confirm these figures.
Private-sector base of about 1,200 Truenat devices already placed, largely standalone labs.

demand_pricing: Government rate contract renewed at realisations similar to last financial year; Q2 average realisations were better than Q1 on product mix, per management.
Management said the revenue gap is about INR100 crore, representing the one month of invoicing shifted into H2.
Government payment cycle: about 60-75 days from invoice to realisation; order supply window is normally 2 months, often delivered within weeks.
Trueamp targets private-sector labs; management contrasted its affordability with BioFire's higher-cost multiplex tests without naming technical differences.
Management said Truenat is on the Global Fund list for Africa and that procurement there follows Global Fund country cycles.
summary.management_tone: Confident on full-year guidance and the timing explanation, but defensive when pressed on the sharp H1 revenue drop and why it was not flagged earlier. Management gave few numbers on veterinary sizing, OptraSCAN commercial traction and export volumes.

qa_highlights.question: Why did revenue fall sharply in H1, given the government tender business is usually steady? Also asked about HPV approval (new devices or existing PHC devices) and the GTM build-out for veterinary and the new platforms.
qa_highlights.answer: Rate-contract renewal negotiations slipped about one month, so that month's invoicing (about INR100 crore) moved into H2; orders are in hand and being shipped. Hepatitis B/C is in the national algorithm and a central procurement is expected as a first-round order. Existing Truenat machines can be used for hepatitis, with new machines procured where needed. Veterinary uses the same platforms, and a team is being built in India and abroad.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the rate-contract delay not flagged in the prior call, and was pricing pressure applied?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the renewal was flagged in the last call but its duration was not known; delay was due to a general body meeting being pushed. Realisations under the new contract are similar to last financial year, and Q2 realisations were better than Q1 on product mix. Management said the fall is about INR100 crore, timing only.

qa_highlights.question: Does the company still expect 25% growth over the next 2-3 years, and what is the 1H/2H split?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance is set on a yearly basis: FY27 target of 25% top-line growth with a 24-25% EBITDA margin, which management says is on track. H1 has typically been 35-45% of full-year revenue; management cited a 40/60 split.

qa_highlights.question: Which veterinary diseases will the 6 assays target, and when will they contribute revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Initial focus is companion animals, with parvo, canine distemper and leptospirosis first; bovine and shrimp come later. Rabies is already in market. Two assays are in development and the rest will follow. Management expects the products in market in FY28. No notifiable veterinary diseases currently.

qa_highlights.question: What is the veterinary molecular market size and Truenat's target share, and who are the main customers?
qa_highlights.answer: No separate molecular market sizing is available; the market is unorganised and testing today is mostly sent to central labs. Management did not give a share target. Initial customers are pet companion animals (dogs and cats) rather than livestock.

qa_highlights.question: Are the three new platforms fully in-house, will royalties apply, and what are the regulatory steps?
qa_highlights.answer: All three platforms were developed in-house with no royalties; Gates Foundation supported Truepoc development with no royalty payable. CDSCO manufacturing and sale licence is about 4-5 months away and launches will be global. Trueamp will start with respiratory, STI, HPV genotyping, sepsis and AMR panels. Management declined to compare technology with BioFire, citing only a different model and cost.

qa_highlights.question: What is the OptraSCAN commercial progress and export outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: OptraSCAN received US FDA approval about 2.5 months ago; some pickup is expected in H2, with real uptake from FY28. Export H2 will see more activity from consumables for the installed base and Global Fund-cycle machine procurement.

risks_watch: Whether the about one-month shift (about INR100 crore) of central and state tender invoicing actually lands in H2 and whether FY27 guidance of 25% growth and 24-25% EBITDA margin holds at Q3.
OptraSCAN's EBITDA loss (INR15 crore in H1) and whether commercial uptake comes in H2 FY27 or only from FY28 as management indicated.
Timing of the CDSCO licence for Truepoc, Trueamp and Truecyte (management said 4-5 months) and the FY28 launch timeline for the veterinary assays.
Government payment cycle of about 60-75 days from invoice to realisation, and receivable days (77 trailing) as a working-capital watch item.
Export ramp-up: H1 exports of about INR120 crore, with management giving no volume targets; monitor Global Fund-driven machine procurement.
Rate-contract pricing: management said realisations are similar to last year, so watch for any change at the next renewal.

adds.what: Automation upgrade (INR72 crore earmarked from IPO proceeds) said to support about 3x the INR1,000 crore top-line level; purchase orders placed
Veterinary X-ray launch with regular and ultra-portable units; already in market
Three new platforms (Truepoc, Trueamp, Truecyte) pending India CDSCO licence about 4-5 months away

growth.why: FY27 ~25% revenue growth and 24-25% EBITDA margin held, H2-loaded after H1 flat at INR667 crore vs INR680 crore; backing is partial (orders in hand, rate contract renewed, automation capex with POs placed, but no quantified order book).

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin 23% in H1 with OptraSCAN loss of INR15 crore (about 2.2% of revenue); FY27 guide of 24-25% needs H2 margin to rise above H1, which depends on the INR100 crore shifted revenue landing in H2 and OptraSCAN losses narrowing.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Management said automation (INR72 crore, POs placed) supports about 3x the INR1,000 crore top line, so no further capex is needed; utilisation cited at about 58% kits and 42% devices.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: H1 revenue flat at INR667 crore vs INR680 crore, but about INR100 crore of invoicing was shifted into H2 and orders are in hand; FY27 25% growth guidance with a 40/60 H1/H2 split implies H2 volume must be strongly up.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is about 58% for kits and 42% for devices, well below the 80% threshold, and management said no further capex is needed for current growth.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Guidance was only maintained (25% growth, 24-25% EBITDA margin) with H1 flat, so a raise is not signalled.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H1 revenue of INR667 crore was flat, and FY27 25% growth needs a steep H2 ramp against a 40/60 split; the shifted INR100 crore must land in H2 and OptraSCAN is loss-making with uptake from FY28.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Truepoc, Trueamp and Truecyte await CDSCO licence about 4-5 months away and six veterinary assays are targeted for FY28; launches will be global, and the call gave no revenue numbers.

rows.label: Hepatitis B/C central procurement as first-round order
rows.why: Hepatitis B/C is in the national algorithm and a central procurement is expected as a first-round order, with existing Truenat machines usable and new machines procured where needed; no size given.

rows.label: Export ramp with Global Fund machine procurement
rows.why: H1 exports were about INR120 crore and management expects more export activity in H2 including Global Fund-driven machine procurement, but gave no volume targets.

rows.label: OptraSCAN commercial pickup
rows.why: FDA approval received about 2.5 months before the call and H1 EBITDA loss was INR15 crore; management expects H2 pickup with meaningful uptake only from FY28.

tone.note: Management was confident on FY27 guidance of 25% growth and 24-25% margin and on the one-month rate-contract timing explanation, but defensive on the flat H1 and why the delay was not flagged earlier; analysts pressed on the revenue drop and the H2 catch-up.
